analysis:
The only change in this PR is a single documentation line in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1687). It adds a row to the table of environment variables that darkbloom start forwards into the LaunchAgent plist. The new row is `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES`, read by `DeadlineAdmissionFixes.environmentKey` in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift. Units 4 and 5 are unchanged base text, and unit 6 contains the surrounding table lines.

This is documentation only. No source, config or code changed in the supplied evidence, so no control was weakened. The row names a scheduling and admission-deadline tuning knob. It does not appear to touch the attestation, authorization, encryption, prefix-cache (T-041) or App Attest (TB-011, T-053) boundaries. Forwarding it affects only the operator's own provider process, and the operator is already within the local trust boundary for the environment-variable tunables listed alongside it. A malicious provider can already change local scheduling behavior, so this adds no new adversary capability. Consumers cannot set provider environment variables.

I could not verify the claim itself. The corresponding Swift change to LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys and the AdmissionRateEstimators implementation are not in the supplied batch. If the code was not changed to match, the doc would be wrong, which is a documentation-accuracy issue and not a security regression. I did not check whether the variable could weaken request deadlines, queueing or fairness (availability), because that code is outside the evidence. The threat model needs no update from this line. A later pass that sees the Swift change should confirm the knob cannot affect admission safety in ways that matter for T-010 or T-029.
